title: Canonical coefficient comparisons preserve the derived adjunction
statement: Let Λ and Λ′ be commutative rings in Type(u+1), φ:Λ→Λ′ a ring homomorphism, and f:Z→W any morphism of schemes. Let Res_Z and Res_W denote the exact restriction functors on bounded below derived categories, and U_f, V_f the canonical inverse- and direct-image comparisons of [lem-sbc-canonical-restrict-scalars-functor-comparisons]. For every M in D⁺(W_et,Λ′), the unit η_f at Res_W(M), followed by Rf_*(U_f(M)) and V_f(f^*M)^{-1}, equals Res_W(η′_f(M)). For every N in D⁺(Z_et,Λ′), f^*(V_f(N)^{-1}), followed by U_f(Rf′_*N) and Res_Z(ε′_f(N)), equals ε_f(Res_Z(N)). These are the unit and counit of the inverse-image/direct-image adjunction used in [sbc-def-base-change-map]; no square or base-change map occurs in either identity.

proof.text: The underived direct-image coefficient comparison is sectionwise identity. The inverse-image comparison is leftAdjointUniq for the composite adjunctions with coefficient coextension. Transpose the unit_leftAdjointUniq_hom_app and leftAdjointUniq_hom_app_counit identities through restriction/coextension to obtain the underived unit and counit comparison identities.

Apply exact derivation to the inverse-image comparison. The direct-image comparison is the canonical right-derived comparison, characterized by the right-derived unit. Compute both derived adjunction identities on bounded below resolutions: the formulas derivedPlus_unit_app_fac and derivedPlus_counit_app_fac reduce them to the underived identities. Restricted injective complexes are direct-image acyclic, so the derived comparison is invertible and can be written with its inverse. Naturality transports from the resolution to every object.
